company_name: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc.

inputs.share_count_basis: Per COMMON share (the HKEX 9901 line trades common shares; 1 NYSE ADS = 10 common shares since 2022-04-08). 1,550,295,803 common shares outstanding at 2026-09-11 (FY2026 20-F / HK annual report, beneficial-ownership note, 9901.HK_Annual_FY2026.txt:7577) + 17.02M dilutive equity awards (FY2026 diluted 1,595,505,635 less basic 1,578,483,794 weighted shares, line 11800-11803) = 1,567.32M fully diluted common shares. Identical to the EDU build's 156.73M ADS-equivalents x 10. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the company is a net repurchaser (1,580.3M -> 1,549.1M shares over FY2026), so the buyback is the cash that keeps the count flat, not extra value.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 20-F / HK annual report (9901.HK_Annual_FY2026.txt): SBC 88.466M (cash-flow add-back; kpis StockBasedComp) + 19.443M cash taxes on net-share-settled equity awards (financing; kpis EquityAwardTaxes). No combined company figure is published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are in USD (the 20-F/HK annual report's primary reporting currency, confirmed from the statement headers; no convenience translation). The HKEX quote is in HKD per common share. All per-share values are built in USD per common share and converted at USD/HKD 7.8413 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-23T20:57Z; fx_rate is model -> quote, i.e. multiply USD by 7.8413 to get HKD). Parity check against the NYSE ADS: EDU US$58.38 (2026-10-23 close) / 10 shares per ADS x 7.8413 = HK$45.78 vs the observed 9901.HK close of HK$46.42 -- a 1.4% HK premium with the HK close ~12 hours earlier, which ties the rate, the direction and the per-common-share basis. HKD is pegged to USD (7.75-7.85), so the bridge is near-static and the real currency exposure is RMB/USD translation inside the USD flows, which is the same for both lines.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T08:08:08Z HKEX regular close (Friday; valuation run Saturday 2026-10-24). Q1 FY2027 results are scheduled for 2026-10-28 before the US open; expect a re-anchor of the FY2027 growth year then.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC; no debt so WACC = cost of equity. 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.0 x 5.0% ERP = 9.2%, + ~1.0pp China country risk premium, + ~1.8pp structural premium for the Cayman/VIE structure (contractual control not equity ownership, HFCAA/PCAOB delisting tail on the NYSE line, capital controls on repatriation) and the education-policy tail evidenced by the 2021 'double reduction' = 12.0%. The HK listing does not lower this: the HK common share is the same Cayman claim on the same VIE contracts; it removes the NYSE-delisting tail for the holder but not the VIE or policy risk, and the ~1.8pp is dominated by the latter. This premium is the ONE place regulatory/structural risk is charged: scenarios model operating outcomes only and all three use the same 12% (no per-scenario WACC). Discounting USD flows at a USD rate then converting at the pegged HKD rate is equivalent to a HKD-built rate within the peg band.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost (learning-centre rent) is already inside operating expenses, OCF and the EBITDA margin, so leases are treated as operating cost and the $848.8M operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A of $178.7M is PP&E/intangible depreciation only (ROU amortization sits in rent). Charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: East Buy (1797.HK) is 55.61% owned; NCI took $41.5M (8%) of FY2026 net income (kpis NetIncomeInclNCI 516.7 vs attributable 475.2). Flows are made attributable by folding ~4-5pp of NCI leakage plus PRC dividend withholding into the 31% cash tax/leakage rate (FY2026 cash tax 168.5M on EBIT 643.3M = 26%). FY0 tie: 643.3 x 0.69 = 444M modelled NOPAT vs ~423M attributable NI ex after-tax non-operating income (475.2 less ~52M after-tax other income/FV/equity-method), within 5%. The minorities' share of existing subsidiary net assets (NCI book $338.1M, mostly East Buy cash consolidated in the pile) is deducted in the equity bridge; that is the stock, the leakage rate is the flow, so NCI is not charged twice.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF + non-US adaptations (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US; adaptations (a2) reporting currency USD vs quote currency HKD, (c) NCI, (d) excluded income / matching asset). New Oriental is an operating education + livestream e-commerce business with no financial-balance-sheet characteristics, so owner-FCF is the right engine. SAME COMPANY AS EDU: 9901.HK is the HKEX secondary listing of the Cayman company whose ADS trades as EDU (1 ADS = 10 common shares); the HK annual report reproduces the 20-F. This is the first valuation of the 9901.HK ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior 9901.HK DCF) but NOT a fresh set of judgments: every driver path, the WACC, the weights, the equity bridge and the owner-FCF anchors are carried over verbatim from research/EDU/Reports/EDU_Drivers.json (2026-10-04), because no new evidence has arrived since -- the FY2026 20-F (2026-09-22) was already the source, Q1 FY2027 is not out until 2026-10-28, and the three 6-Ks filed since (2026-10-08, 2026-10-13) are routine. The only changes are mechanical: per-common-share divisor (x10 shares), HKD quote currency with the fx bridge, and the price. Deliberately unchanged: growth path (would move on Q1 FY2027 print vs the +14-18% guidance), margin path (would move on FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin trajectory), SBC%/D&A/capex/tax paths (no new disclosure), WACC (would move only on a structural event: VIE ruling, PCAOB access change, policy directive), weights (would move on East Buy GMV trend or demographics evidence). FY0 = FY2026 (May-26). Owner FCF = reported FCF 780.2 (OCF 1,027.1 - capex 246.9) - SBC incl. equity-award taxes 107.9 - interest income 76.9 = 595.4. Interest income is stripped because net cash ($5.56B) is ~9x the FCF base; the engine builds from EBIT (operating income ex 'other income'), so interest, investment FV gains and equity-method losses all sit outside the flows and their source assets (cash pile, long-term investments) are in the bridge. Net cash = cash 1,821.2 + term deposits (current 919.5 + non-current 447.3) 1,366.8 + short-term investments 2,372.3; restricted cash (275.3, PRC prepaid-tuition supervision) excluded; unsecured senior notes fully repaid in FY2026 so total debt 0 (the Metrics.csv TotalDebt FY2026 = 0 agrees). Deferred revenue $2.24B (customer prepayments) is NOT deducted: it is a perpetual operating float while the business is a going concern; per the parser's warning it is NOT extrapolated as a share of revenue -- the deferred-revenue inflow is modelled as wc_capture (30%) on the revenue CHANGE, so it shrinks as growth decelerates and reverses on the bear path's revenue dips. FY2022 (double-reduction loss, OCF -1,280) is excluded from every anchor and CAGR base. Base year-1 owner FCF ~10.6% of revenue vs FY2026 actual 10.5% (595.4/5,661): no one-off is being carried forward. Shareholder returns: FY2026 buyback cash $230.9M and US$0.12/common share ordinary dividend; FY2027 plan ~$300M dividend + up to $200M buyback (~5.5% of the ~US$9.3B market cap), executable in either the ADS or the HK common-share market. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (count held flat, SBC expensed). Risk is charged once, in WACC; probability weights reflect operating dispersion only.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term investments at book (equity-method and FV investees; their losses/gains are excluded from the flows)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 balance sheet at 2026-05-31, Long-term investments, net 383,063k

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (minorities' share of consolidated net assets, chiefly East Buy's 44.4% outside holders)
Dividend payable (declared FY2026 second instalment, already owed)

expected_9901_hkd_per_share.note: EDU weighted US$88.12/ADS / 10 x 7.8413 = HK$69.10; the 9901.HK build must land within rounding of this, because the drivers are identical and only the divisor and currency differ. Any larger gap is an engine or fx-direction error, not a valuation view.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2021-FY2026, spans the double-reduction shock and recovery)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.3% / -2.9%) diverges >30% from revenue (23.6% / 5.8%) and EPS (41.3% / 8.4%). Equity is depressed by the FY2022 write-downs and by $930M of buybacks plus dividends FY2023-26, so it is not a usable growth anchor. The 3-year revenue and EPS CAGRs measure a rebound off the FY2023 trough, not a repeatable rate; the 5-year revenue CAGR spans the shock and is used as the through-cycle reference. Forward growth is anchored on FY2027 guidance (+14-18%) decelerating, not on any historical CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are basis-invariant and identical to the EDU build. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - interest income, FY2021-FY2026 (FY2022 excluded as n/m). Owner FCF has gone sideways (FY2023 621.5 -> FY2026 595.4) while revenue grew 89%: the FY2023 base was flattered by a deferred-revenue rebuild and $114M of interest income on a larger pile, and FY2024-26 capex stepped up for learning-centre and East Buy expansion. SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR (-1.4%) is close to reported (-2.0%), so SBC is not the cause; the gap is margin mix (East Buy e-commerce is lower-margin than tutoring). EPS here is per common share (US$0.30 FY2026, US$0.20 FY2021 per the Metrics.csv).

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +15% sits inside the +14-18% guidance band (lower half: guidance is at current USD/RMB and the overseas-consulting segment is soft). Decelerates as non-academic tutoring city roll-out matures and as China's shrinking school-age cohorts (births ~17.9M 2016 -> ~9M 2023) reach the K-9 years from ~FY2029. Carried over from EDU 2026-10-04; re-judge on the 2026-10-28 Q1 FY2027 print.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 adj. EBITDA (op income 643.3 + SBC 88.5 + D&A 178.7) = 16.1%; non-GAAP op margin rose 11.3% -> 13.0% FY2025-26. Base adds ~2.4pp over four years to a 18.5% plateau (~15% non-GAAP op margin), below pre-crackdown tutoring economics because East Buy e-commerce dilutes mix.
base.wc_capture_rationale: Prepaid tuition: deferred revenue rose 288M on 761M revenue growth in FY2026 (38%), 30% FY2025, 34% FY2024; 30% used on the revenue CHANGE, never on the revenue level.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex 4.4% of revenue (246.9M), FY2024-25 4.9-5.8%; learning-centre and East Buy offline-store build tapering to 4.0% (still above 3.3% D&A, i.e. growth capex persists).
base.cash_tax_rationale: 26% cash tax on EBIT FY2026 (25% PRC statutory, some HNTE relief offset by non-deductible items) + PRC dividend withholding on upstreamed profit + ~4-5pp East Buy NCI leakage = 31% combined attributable leakage; ties FY0 NOPAT to attributable NI within 5%.

scenario_narratives.base: New Oriental delivers FY2027 near the lower half of its +14-18% guidance, then decelerates to mid-single digits as the non-academic K-12 tutoring roll-out (~60 cities, >1M quarterly enrollments) matures, domestic adult/university test prep keeps compounding, overseas study consulting stays flat-to-low-growth and East Buy grows with Douyin GMV but at thin margins. Operating leverage and cost discipline lift adj. EBITDA margin from 16.1% to ~18.5% by FY2031 and it plateaus there. The shrinking school-age cohort caps late-decade growth at 3-4%. The HK common share receives exactly one-tenth of the per-ADS economics (dividend US$0.12/share FY2026, ~US$300M FY2027 plan).
scenario_narratives.bull: Guidance is beaten (+18%) as non-academic tutoring and intelligent learning devices keep growing 20%+, East Buy's private-label mix and offline stores in learning centres push its margin up, and overseas consulting recovers with easing visa/geopolitical frictions. Margins return toward pre-2021 tutoring economics (~20.5% adj. EBITDA), and growth stays high-single-digit through FY2031 as New Oriental takes share from sub-scale local tutors exiting under compliance costs.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 misses guidance (+11%) as East Buy GMV churns on Douyin traffic-allocation changes and host attrition, overseas consulting shrinks on US/UK visa tightening, and price competition in non-academic tutoring (TAL, Gaotu, local operators) caps pricing. From FY2030 the halving of China's birth cohort reaches primary/middle-school ages and revenue stalls then dips, which also unwinds part of the deferred-revenue float through the negative wc_capture on falling revenue; margins erode to ~15% as learning-centre leases and teacher costs prove sticky. This is an operating bear: a renewed 2021-style policy shock is charged in the 12% WACC, not here.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Carried over from the EDU build (same company, no new evidence). Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): China's birth cohort has roughly halved since 2016 and reaches the core K-12 non-academic customer base inside the forecast window, and East Buy depends on a single platform (Douyin) for traffic -- both operating, not regulatory, risks. Base 50%: guidance is explicit and deferred revenue (+14.8%) supports it. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs tutoring growth, East Buy margin and an overseas-consulting recovery to go right together. Regulatory/VIE-structure risk is NOT in these weights; it is charged once in the WACC premium.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on attributable USD flows, SBC fully expensed, share count flat, interest income stripped with the $5.56B liquid pile added back in the bridge, converted to HKD per common share at the pegged rate. The valuation hinges on two things the price already disputes: whether the cash pile is worth $1 per $1 to an offshore holder (it sits largely onshore behind a VIE and capital controls) and whether a 12% USD discount rate is enough for a business the state restructured overnight in 2021. Net cash alone is ~US$3.55/share = ~HK$27.8 of a ~HK$46 price. The HK line is the same claim as the ADS with the NYSE-delisting tail removed; it should trade at ADS parity, and it does (1.4% premium on the parity check).
key_risks_to_valuation: Education policy: the 2021 'double reduction' precedent shows a single directive can remove most of the revenue base; charged via the WACC premium, not modelled as a scenario.

VIE structure: HK common shareholders, like ADS holders, own a Cayman shell with contractual (not equity) control of PRC operating entities; a Foreign Investment Law reinterpretation could force an unwind.

Cash pile accessibility: ~$5.56B of cash/deposits/short-term investments is counted at face value; repatriation to offshore holders incurs PRC dividend withholding and is subject to SAFE controls. Deferred revenue of $2.24B is customer prepayments funding part of that pile.
Demographics: births fell from ~17.9M (2016) to ~9M (2023); the K-9 cohort shrinks through the 2030s.
East Buy: single-platform (Douyin) dependency, host concentration, and 44% minority leakage of its profits.
RMB/USD translation: all revenue is RMB, reported in USD; the HKD peg passes this through unchanged to the HK holder.
HK-line liquidity: the secondary listing is thinner than the ADS; wider spreads and transient deviations from ADS parity, though the fungibility mechanism caps them.
